description: Run the project's TypeScript/JavaScript test runner (Vitest, Jest, or Angular's `ng test`) with coverage enabled, then read the exact coverage percentages from the generated `coverage/coverage-summary.json` (falling back to `coverage/lcov.info`'s `LF`/`LH`/`BRF`/`BRH` records via `awk` when the summary is missing or a specific file's row isn't in it) — reporting line/branch percentage totals, per-file percentages scoped to the given selector, and the uncovered line ranges (collapsed from consecutive `DA:<line>,0` records) for files under the bar. Also recognizes NestJS (`@nestjs/core` — the `test:cov` setup, i.e. Vitest + `@vitest/coverage-v8` on ESM, Jest `--coverage` on CommonJS — measured from the `*.spec.ts` unit suite only, with `*.module.ts`/`main.ts` wiring files excluded so they don't drag the number down) and Next.js (`next` — Vitest v8 coverage or Jest via `next/jest`; Playwright end-to-end tests are never run for coverage and never counted) and React Native for both toolchains (`expo` with the `jest-expo` preset, `metro` with `@react-native/jest-preset` or the legacy `react-native` preset — Jest's built-in coverage, with the native `android/`/`ios/` projects, `.expo/`, the `index.js`/`index.ts` registration entry, Metro/Babel/Jest/ESLint/Prettier config files, and test files excluded, and Maestro/Detox device e2e never run or counted). Invoke as `/iru-typescript-coverage [scope]`, where `[scope]` is a file path, a directory, or a name pattern — the same selector syntax as the `iru-typescript-test` skill's — or with no argument to run the whole suite and report whole-project coverage. Detects the test runner (Vitest, Jest, or Angular's `@angular/build:unit-test` builder) and package manager the same way `iru-typescript-test` does, and reports "coverage not wired" (naming the missing package/config) instead of a false 0%/100% when the coverage provider isn't installed. Use whenever the user wants to check, or verify a bar (e.g. "at least 80% line coverage") for, a TypeScript/JavaScript file, directory, or the whole project, instead of eyeballing a runner's console output.
